theory: Astra round-6 section 3: a single GPU broker owns fleet GPU execution exclusively; requests wait in a BOUNDED broker queue with three distinct timeout states (queue deadline / model-load timeout after admission / inference timeout after readiness) so a deferred request is visibly deferred; captures and judges are scheduled by deadline with aging so neither starves; judge requests batch under a capped batch duration; the judge service preloads one model with one parallel request AFTER taking the reservation, retains it through a bounded batch, and unloads BEFORE release; training runs under a durable keeper whose lifetime is independent of the broker -- a broker restart reconnects, never kills, never duplicates; a passed expected-end keeps the reservation occupied until completion is verified; a lost heartbeat means OWNERSHIP UNCERTAIN, never a second owner.
prereg: record.md (this directory), committed before any code; falsifiers = Astra's GPU-broker rejection conditions (overlapping exclusives, lost-heartbeat second owner, queue wait mislabeled as model failure, broker restart duplicating/killing the keeper) + this lane's measurements (queue latency percentiles, model-load latency, batch amortization)
